source_observed_tokens: PLOS article data-availability statement links the study to GEO accession GSE77451.
PLOS Supporting Information identifies S3 as an Excel file listing cycling transcripts in LNds, LNvs, DN1s and TH neurons.
The article reports two independent six-timepoint circadian RNA collections per group, sampled at four-hour intervals in light:dark conditions.
The article defines HC cyclers as passing both JTK_cycle and F24; it reports JTK p<0.05 and F24 score>0.5 plus amplitude and average-read filters.
The paper narrative reports 249 LNv, 303 LNd and 185 DN1 HC cyclers; S3 parsing finds 252, 303 and 185 unique HC symbols, respectively.
The paper describes LNv as mixed PDF-positive small and large cells, LNd as including the fifth PDF-negative s-LNv, and DN1 as a subset.
source_observation_note: Opened the primary PLOS article, checked its Methods, cell-group descriptions, HC-count statement and S3 description, then downloaded and parsed the official S3 workbook. The exact-symbol audit preserves one unresolved LNv mismatch: 252 unique HC symbols in S3 versus 249 in the article narrative. It does not select or correct either source value.

analysis_context.time_system: LD entrainment with source-reported ZT. LNv/LNd timepoints are ZT2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22; DN1 timepoints are ZT3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23.
analysis_context.experimental_unit: Pooled isolated-neuron library in the source study; the candidate audit operates on author-reported gene-symbol rows, not independent fly-level observations.
analysis_context.normalization_status: No expression values or rhythm statistics were recomputed. The report preserves author-reported S3 calls and metrics; the paper describes ESAT normalization relative to the maximum signal within each six-timepoint set.
analysis_context.biological_unit_limitations: The published sampling description gives approximately 50-100 isolated neurons per sample but does not identify individual flies in S3. The LNv group mixes s-/l-LNv, LNd includes the fifth PDF-negative s-LNv, and DN1 is a subset. Transcript cycling is not protein/current/membrane-potential or causal-behavior evidence.
